title: Multiparty Clique lower bounds in compression games
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
formal: Do there exist a constant \(\varepsilon>0\) and an integer round bound \(r(N)\to\infty\) such that every nonuniform, deterministic, polynomial-party \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\)-compression protocol family deciding Clique with at most \(r(N)\) rounds has cost \(\Omega(N^\varepsilon)\)? Here \(N\) is the graph’s number of vertices. In each round, Alice sends messages to independent computationally unrestricted Bobs, receives their replies, and eventually computes the answer herself with an \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\) circuit. Cost is the sum over rounds of the maximum length of an Alice-to-Bob message in that round.

source_formulation.text: We conjecture that such a lower bound holds for the Clique function.
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 6

why: This asks whether many unrestricted helpers can compensate for Alice’s constant-depth computation using short messages and an increasing number of interactions. The source connects a positive answer for Clique to a major nonuniform circuit lower bound. The unusual communication measure makes precise model recovery essential to that connection.
status_note: The conjecture is explicit in the 2015 primary source. Its proved fixed-round Majority results and logarithmic-depth simulation do not settle the selected growing-round Clique bound. Bounded subsequent-result searches through 2026-09-15 identified no resolution, but this dated review does not certify present openness exhaustively.

progress.text: Oliveira and Santhanam define the multiparty model in Section 2 and state the growing-round Clique conjecture on printed page 129.

Corollary 5.6 gives the \(n^{O(1/r)}\) compression upper bound for nonuniform logarithmic-depth functions for every fixed \(r\). The paper’s established Majority lower bounds do not close the selected Clique question.

category_assignment.reason: The core model is communication by circuit-restricted players to a referee.

importance.reason: The model isolates whether interaction with unrestricted computation can overcome constant-depth limitations at low communication cost. The conjectured Clique bound would separate NP from nonuniform logarithmic-depth circuits, giving this precise communication question consequences far beyond a single compression scheme.
importance.basis: Individual review of Oliveira–Santhanam Sections 1.2, 2 and 5, especially Corollary 5.6; importance is an editorial assessment of its structural and circuit-complexity consequences.

sentences: Alice sees a graph and a requested clique size, but her computation is limited to polynomial-size constant-depth Boolean circuits.
She can exchange messages with polynomially many unrestricted helpers, each of whom sees only its own conversation.
Alice must compute the correct final answer on every input.
Communication cost sums the longest message from Alice in each round, and the question asks for a polynomial lower bound even under a growing round budget.
The source shows that such a Clique lower bound would separate NP from nonuniform logarithmic-depth circuits.

definitions: For each integer \(N\ge2\), the input consists of the \(\binom N2\) adjacency bits of a simple undirected graph \(G\) on \([N]\), listed in lexicographic order of pairs \(i<j\), followed by \(\ell=\lceil\log_2(N+1)\rceil\) bits encoding a nonnegative integer \(k\) in ordinary most-significant-bit-first binary. The input length is \(L_N=\binom N2+\ell\). Clique is 1 if \(0\le k\le N\) and some \(k\)-vertex set has every pair joined by an edge; it is 0 when \(k>N\). The empty set makes the answer 1 for \(k=0\). Alice receives all input bits, while \(b_N\ge1\) Bobs receive no input. A protocol has a fixed number \(R_N\le r(N)\) of rounds. In round \(t\), Alice simultaneously sends a fixed-length binary string \(a_{t,j}\) to each Bob \(j\). Each Bob replies with a fixed-length binary string \(z_{t,j}\). Message lengths and all strategies are fixed before the input is known; empty strings are permitted. Bob \(j\)’s reply is an arbitrary deterministic function of the sequence \(a_{1,j},\ldots,a_{t,j}\), with no computational restriction. Bobs cannot communicate with each other or observe other Bobs’ messages. Each message \(a_{t,j}\) is computed by a Boolean circuit using the original input and all messages in earlier completed rounds. After the final replies, an additional circuit at Alice computes the single output bit from the input and the complete transcript. All of Alice’s circuits use only AND and OR gates of arbitrary finite fan-in, unary NOT gates, and constants. There are constants \(d\in\mathbb N\), \(A>0\) and \(a\in\mathbb N\), fixed across \(N\) for the protocol family, such that every Alice circuit has depth at most \(d\), and the sum of their gate, wire, input and output counts, the number \(b_N\) of Bobs, and the total number of transmitted bits are each at most \(A(N+1)^a\). Reply bits are not charged to communication cost, but remain subject to these polynomial length bounds. Alice’s circuits and all Bob functions may depend arbitrarily on \(N\); no uniform construction is required. No player uses randomness. Correctness means the output equals Clique on every input of length \(L_N\). Define \(c_\Pi(N)=\sum_{t=1}^{R_N}\max_{1\le j\le b_N}|a_{t,j}|\). The target quantifiers are \(\exists\varepsilon>0\;\exists r:\mathbb N_{\ge2}\to\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) with \(r(N)\to\infty\) and \(r(N)\le\lceil\log_2(N+1)\rceil\), such that \(\forall\Pi\) in the specified model deciding Clique, \(\exists C_\Pi>0\;\exists N_\Pi\ge2\;\forall N\ge N_\Pi,\ c_\Pi(N)\ge C_\Pi N^\varepsilon\). The constants governing polynomial circuit size, constant depth and the number of parties are arbitrary and may depend on \(\Pi\), while \(\varepsilon,r\) are chosen before \(\Pi\).
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the quantified lower-bound statement, or a complete Lean-checked proof of its logical negation. The affirmative proof must cover every polynomial-size constant-depth Alice family and every collection of unrestricted Bob strategies, for the stated growing round budget and some exponent independent of the protocol family. A fixed-round lower bound whose exponent tends to zero as the chosen round count grows does not establish the target. Bounds on the total sum of all parties’ message lengths, a single-Bob model, average-case correctness or a different function do not establish this Clique statement.

context_blocks.text: The selected sentence follows the source’s conjecture of a polynomial communication lower bound with a growing number of rounds. This card interprets it as the existence of one growing round budget and one positive exponent that work against every polynomial-size constant-depth protocol family, with the lower-bound constant and starting length allowed to depend on the family.

The source uses input-bit length \(n\). This statement fixes a standard graph-and-threshold encoding and uses vertex count \(N\), with \(L_N=\Theta(N^2)\); a fixed positive polynomial exponent remains a fixed positive polynomial exponent under this normalization. The growing budget is capped at \(\lceil\log_2(N+1)\rceil\): existence of a lower bound for any growing budget also entails it for a smaller growing budget. Aggregate polynomial circuit and transcript bounds agree with the source’s polynomial resources in this round range.

In the multiparty model, Alice computes the final answer. An unrestricted Bob does not act as a referee who receives everyone’s messages. The Bobs are independent helpers with access only to their respective conversations with Alice, and only messages from Alice contribute to the stated cost.

Corollary 5.6 states that every function in \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}/\mathrm{poly}\) has polynomial-party \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\) compression games of cost \(n^{O(1/r)}\) for each fixed positive integer \(r\). Here \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}/\mathrm{poly}\) means Boolean functions computed by nonuniform polynomial-size, bounded-fan-in circuits of depth \(O(\log n)\).

The paper consequently identifies the conjectured Clique lower bound as sufficient to separate \(\mathrm{NP}\) from \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}/\mathrm{poly}\). Its Majority bounds have round-dependent exponents and do not establish the required fixed exponent for Clique with an unbounded round budget.
